cards.text: The fight against Midian is on, and Gideon, the man leading Israel against them, is right in the middle of it. Then the men of Ephraim, one of Israel's tribes, march up to him. And friend, they did NOT come to say congratulations.

cards.question: Why are the men of Ephraim so upset with Gideon?

answers.text: He didn't call them to fight Midian
He kept the plunder for himself
He put Manasseh in charge of them

cards.question: The men of Ephraim argue with Gideon fiercely.

cards.text: Gideon could fire right back at them. Instead, with angry men in his face, he asks them a question about GRAPES: aren't the gleanings of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer, his own clan (Judges 6:11)?

cards.question: Gideon reminds the men of Ephraim what God delivered into their hand. What is it?

answers.text: Oreb and Zeeb the princes of Midian
Zebah and Zalmunna the kings of Midian
The whole camp of the Midianites

cards.text: Then Gideon asks them, “What was I able to do compared to you?” That's somebody yelling at you for leaving them off the group chat, and you reply, “Are you kidding? This chat is DEAD without you.”

cards.question: Once Gideon gives the men of Ephraim the credit, their anger against him ___.

cards.text: Now Gideon and his three hundred men cross the Jordan, and they're STILL chasing. They come to the town of Succoth.

cards.question: Gideon asks the men of Succoth for ___ because his troops are ___.

cards.text: He tells them he's still chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian. Two KINGS, friend, being chased by three hundred guys who'd trade their swords for one cookie right now.

cards.question: The leaders of Succoth are happy to feed Gideon's tired men.

cards.text: They ask, “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your army?” That's asking your boss for a pen and hearing, “Finish the project FIRST, then we'll talk about pens.”

cards.question: Gideon answers Succoth with a warning. When does he say he'll deal with them?

answers.text: When the LORD hands him the two kings
When the men of Ephraim catch up
When the barley harvest is over

cards.text: Gideon warns them, “…I will tear your flesh with the thorns and briers of the wilderness!”
From there Gideon goes up to Penuel and asks them for bread too. Friend, I bet he's thinking, surely THIS town has a heart.

cards.question: How do the men of Penuel answer Gideon's request for his troops?

answers.text: They refuse him just like Succoth
They give his men bread and water
They send men to join the chase

cards.question: Gideon has a warning for Penuel too. What does he say he'll tear down when he returns in triumph?

cards.text: Meanwhile, Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian, are in Karkor with about fifteen thousand men. That's all that's left of the armies of the people of the east.

cards.question: Only about fifteen thousand men are left. How many swordsmen from the armies of the east have already fallen?

cards.text: Then Gideon goes up by the caravan route east of Nobah and Jogbehah. Fifteen thousand men are out there, and the three hundred guys nobody would even give bread to are the ones doing the CHASING.

cards.question: Gideon's attack on the army at Karkor takes them by surprise.
When Zebah and Zalmunna flee, what happens to the two kings of Midian?

cards.text: Gideon routs their entire army. On his way back along the Ascent of Heres, he captures a young man from Succoth and questions him.

cards.question: The young man writes down for Gideon the ___ of Succoth's seventy-seven leaders and elders.
Gideon goes back to Succoth, the town that wouldn't give his men bread. Who does he show them?

cards.text: Gideon tells the men of Succoth, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me…” and he brings up their question about the kings' hands. That's walking back into the meeting that laughed at your plan, holding the proof, and Gideon's proof is two KINGS.
Then he takes the elders of the city, and using the thorns and briers of the wilderness, he disciplines the men of Succoth.

cards.question: Gideon leaves the tower of Penuel standing.

cards.text: He pulls down the tower of Penuel and kills the men of the city. Next, Gideon asks Zebah and Zalmunna, “What kind of men did you kill at Tabor?”

cards.question: How do Zebah and Zalmunna describe the men they killed at Tabor?
The kings say those men were like Gideon, “each one resembling the son of a king.” Gideon tells them the men killed at Tabor were his ___.

cards.text: Then Gideon tells them, “As surely as the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you.”

cards.question: When Gideon tells Jether, his firstborn son, to kill the kings, Jether draws his sword.

cards.text: Jether is fearful, because he's still a youth.
Then Zebah and Zalmunna say, “Get up and kill us yourself, for as the man is, so is his strength.” So Gideon gets up and kills them.

cards.question: After that, Gideon takes something from the necks of the kings' camels. What is it?

cards.text: And that's where we'll stop for now, friend. Gideon's story isn't finished, not even close.
